1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

sentences.text: The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 14 with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of share in the land bearing Khasra no.40//11/1(104) 36//2 (416) 29//19 (412) 22(416) total land admeasuring 15 Bigha 08 Biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that the petitioners were the absolute owner as well as in cultivatory possession of the said land and till the date of taking over the possession of the said land.
6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation and as such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) the learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.

The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and Shri Kaptan Singh vs Union Of India on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150039912/
2 potentiality of the land".

It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the LAC no. 115 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 14 said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 12.07.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.

(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 14 allottees of the residential plot/flats.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards,
therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after affixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.

The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2 3 Shri Kaptan Singh vs Union Of India on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150039912/
3 commercial crops in a year.

sentences.text: The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Rani Khera and the cost of the said land is Rs.
500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award (ix)

The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by be said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.

It is LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

sentences.text: (x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with 30% solatium and interest @ 24% per annum with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners are also claiming an alternative plot of reasonable size and Rs. 2 lakh for the tubewell, compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/
for standing crops and the value of trees @ Rs. 5,000/ each.
7.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of construction of structure, which is placed without the sanction of law and in terms of section 4 notification there were no structure, tree, well on the said land.
The said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colony and can be used for agricultural purposes only.
The ld. LAC categorised the land into two categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.
The ld. LAC considered value of land as detailed in the sale deeds registered in the office of SubRegistrar in proximity to the notification.

The ld. LAC has considered the sale transaction of similar land situated in the vicinity and the small pieces of land in square yards cannot be compared with the huge land covered under the acquisition, therefore, the registered LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No.

8.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for for the year 2001  2002 which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
The ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block A".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 57 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 3,40,000 per acre from the market value of "Block A"
category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 12,30,000 per acre,
and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for different categories of land besides other statutory benefits.
It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioners are misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the said sale LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 14 deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
11. The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
As per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award, reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

It is stated that DDA is not liable to pay compensation as the said land has not been taken over by the DDA either due to stay by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi or has been handed over to DDA and subsequently taken back by land and building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.

The Award passed by ld.
LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld.
LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioners are not entitled for grant of any enhanced compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioners in reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioners is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioners is liable to be dismissed with cost.
13.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 16.09.2013 :  ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount ?

2. Relief.
14.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.
ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.text: Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 15.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issuewise findings and determination are as under :  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ?
16.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.

sentences.text: Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

20. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
RELIEF 22.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards,
therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after affixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
Therefore, the LAC no. 115 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Kaptan Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
